content.user_title: Execute Development Plans with Parallel Subagents
content.value_statement: Large development plans are slow and difficult to coordinate across concurrent tasks. This skill schedules Sparky subagents, validates results, integrates changes, and updates the source plan.
actual_capabilities: Parses task sections and optional task subsets from Markdown plan files.
Builds context packs with canonical paths, naming rules, and shared-file information.
Schedules up to 12 Sparky subagents through a continuously refilled worker pool.
Validates each completed task before scheduling the next pending task.
Reconciles parallel changes, adds tests, runs validation, and fixes integration failures.
Updates plan status and produces a structured execution summary.
limitations: Requires explicit invocation, an accessible Markdown plan, and a supported Sparky subagent role.
Ignores dependency metadata, so users must ensure tasks are suitable for parallel execution.
Cannot guarantee conflict-free edits when concurrent tasks modify shared files.
Requires subagents to create local commits, which changes repository history during execution.

use_cases.title: Deliver a Feature Plan
use_cases.description: Execute a complete feature plan in parallel, validate each task, and integrate the resulting changes.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering leads managing multi-task feature delivery

use_cases.title: Complete Selected Maintenance Tasks
use_cases.description: Run only chosen task identifiers from a larger maintenance plan while preserving shared naming and path constraints.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Test and Integration Work
use_cases.description: Distribute implementation tasks, resolve cross-task conflicts, and run a final regression pass before completion.

prompt_templates.title: Execute a Complete Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: /super-swarm-spark plans/release-plan.md. Execute every task, validate each result, update the plan, and provide the execution summary.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for running one complete development plan

prompt_templates.title: Run Selected Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: /super-swarm-spark plans/auth-plan.md T1 T2 T4. Run only these tasks, preserve canonical paths, and report deferred validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused workflow for a task subset

prompt_templates.title: Protect Shared Files
prompt_templates.prompt: /super-swarm-spark plans/api-plan.md. Highlight tasks sharing files, enforce the plan's canonical names, and reconcile conflicts during integration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for plans with overlapping file ownership

prompt_templates.title: Enforce Full Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: /super-swarm-spark plans/migration-plan.md --tasks T3 T5 T7. Complete the subset, add regression tests, rerun failures, and document blockers with evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow requiring targeted execution and rigorous validation

output: Completed six assigned tasks with a maximum of six active workers.
Resolved one shared-file conflict during integration.
Added profile validation coverage and completed the required test run.
Updated the plan with task logs and modified file paths.

output_examples.input: Run tasks T3 and T7 from plans/auth-plan.md.
output: Completed T3 and T7 while leaving all other tasks unchanged.
Validated both task acceptance criteria and recorded their local commits.
Reported one deferred integration test with its blocking dependency.

best_practices: Use plans with explicit task identifiers, canonical file paths, acceptance criteria, and validation steps.
Choose task subsets that can proceed independently when the plan contains strict dependencies.
Review local commits, plan updates, and final test results before sharing the branch.
anti_patterns: Do not launch a vague plan that omits file ownership or expected outputs.
Do not parallelize tightly ordered migrations or tasks with unresolved prerequisites.
Do not allow multiple tasks to invent different names for the same file or feature.

faq.question: How is this skill triggered?
faq.answer: Invoke super-swarm-spark explicitly and provide a Markdown plan path. You may also provide selected task identifiers.

faq.question: How many subagents can run concurrently?
faq.answer: The required scheduling policy permits up to 12 active Sparky subagents.

faq.question: Can I execute only part of a plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide task identifiers, and the skill filters the parsed plan to those tasks.

faq.question: How does the skill reduce filename conflicts?
faq.answer: It sends each subagent canonical paths, naming constraints, and information about tasks that touch shared files.

faq.question: Does the skill run tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It requests task validation and performs a final integration pass with tests and failure resolution.

faq.question: Does the skill modify Git history?
faq.answer: Yes. Its task template requires each subagent to create a local commit for its own changes and never push.
